_about: Stage 2 (2026-09-08): which equipment GLB drops at which house socket, and what to hide when it does. Every inspection GLB carries its own scene context (a wall, a floor, grass, soil, a closet) so it can be inspected alone; in the house that context is hidden and the house provides it. The loader drops the model at the socket's world matrix (socket local +Y = front of the equipment), then applies yaw (degrees about the up axis) because most models were built with their front toward -Y and their wall side at +Y. Models live in the app under public/models and in the viewer under electric_tank_water_heater/viewer/models. Alternates share a socket; only the default is placed unless the house config picks the alternate. 'replaces' names the house fix_ placeholder boxes the loader hides when the model is present. 'offset' is a model-space translation (metres, applied before yaw) that moves the model's own wall plane onto the origin, so a socket placed on the house wall face lands the model against that wall: M = socket × Rz(yaw) × T(offset).

move_note: move: {node: [dx, dy, dz]} in model space (Blender axes, metres); the walk page and assemble_house.py shift that node
stream_note: stream meshes are NOT hidden by pattern any more: the walk page hides them at load and shows them while a run / on clip is playing, so a faucet actually runs water
flame_note: flames, igniter_glow and burner_flame are NOT hidden by pattern any more: their builders rest them at scale 0.001 and the fire_up clip brings them up, so a click actually lights the burner (Jake 2026-09-11)
reveal_note: reveal: {trigger: [parts a click on toggles it], hide: [model parts that go away while open], show: [model parts shown while open, even ones the placement hides], bore: [model parts whose world box is cut out of every house mesh it overlaps while open]}. walk.js reveal().
